utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there was one preliminary matter the Prosecution wishes to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and good morning. Your Honours, could I ask that we go into private session for this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Meanwhile I'll put a few things on the record. First, in relation to the 26th, 92 bis motion, we have granted the Defence's request to respond to the Prosecution's 26th, 92 bis motion, but in Court we gave the wrong date for the new dead-line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That causes us now to the following. When, on the 16th of May we granted the Defence request for the extension but provided the wrong date for that new dead-line, we hereby decide that we granted the request but the new dead-line is now set as the 31st of May, 2013. And a second matter I would like to put on the record is that on the 17th of May the Defence has requested a 60-day extension for the dead-lines to respond to the Prosecution's 27th, 92 bis motion, and the new dead-line is hereby set at the 16th of July of this year. Good morning to you, Mr. Trivic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, before we continue I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Before Mr. Lukic continues his cross-examination, I would briefly like to deal with a matter which arose yesterday. On the record we saw that you had referred to the evacuation of the Muslim population from Potocari and a few minutes later you denied to have said any of such thing, and I even suggested to you that you might consider that you may have said it but that -- that you do not exclude for that possibility. You insisted on it being verified. It has been verified. That means the audio has been listened to and the translation has been verified. This is what you said: "Thank you. During that day at the meeting and during the dinner, there was no talk of prisoners of war or disarmed enemy forces. All that was discussed was the evacuation of the population, evacuation of the Muslim population from Potocari." That is what you said and that was how it was translated to us. No need further to discuss that denying a couple of minutes later that you had said this was a useless exercise. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed. By the way, does the Defence want a full report, official memo, or is this -- this is what we received by e-mail and that is -- a formal memo would contain the same content.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If it's not too big hassle for Your Honours, we would like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll ask for an official memo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Shall we briefly just go back to this that His Honour, Judge Orie just read out. Can you explain it now, whether this was discussed, whether this was not discussed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Lukic or the witness. They were speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. If you speak at the same time, then there will be no transcript and no translation. Mr. Lukic, if you would please re-introduce your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript I shall repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us now at this meeting whether civilians were discussed, whether transportation was discussed at all, whether prisoners of war were discussed, disarmed enemy forces? Could you please explain this to us if you can?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the permission of the Chamber, I would like to explain. Obviously, it is necessary to say which meeting this was. Yesterday, I believe, as I gave this some thought during the break when this misunderstanding occurred, you asked about the meeting in Fontana, and I was not in Fontana on the 12th of July. Hence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no way. There is no way that the questions were about the meeting in Fontana. The questions were about the headquarters, where the meeting took place, the dinner after that, and not Fontana. I think I said this yesterday. If one of the persons in this courtroom misspoke a few minutes later, you -- that doesn't change the subject of the question and a clear subject of the answer. So such an explanation is not something the Chamber is interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I try to answer your question now. That evening at the meeting at the command of the Bratunac Brigade on the evening of the 12th, there was no reference to evacuation except for the part that General Mladic dealt with as the provision of fuel for the evacuation of the population and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have been using a term here and the Judges asked you about that as well. Why do you say "disarmed enemy forces"? Somewhere in your statements I found the source of that term, so could you explain that to us. What is the source of that term? Who is it that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The source of that term is what General Dwight Eisenhower did - the commander of the Allied Forces in 1945 - vis-a-vis the German forces in the occupation zone when -- in the area where -- that was under his control. He declared these forces "disarmed enemy forces" rather than "prisoners of war." They were found as such as they were withdrawing from the areas that they were trying to occupy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, we interrupted my line of questioning when I asked you about Nova Kasaba. We established that you travelled by car and I was not clear enough when I asked whether you had gotten out of the car. I should have asked you whether you got out of the car in Nova Kasaba. You said that you did not leave the car at all, but let us just confirm now whether you left the car in Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not leave the vehicle that I was in. I did not leave it in Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you did not leave the car, would you agree with me that you did not have a good view of the sports ground and you could not assess the number of people who were there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not estimate the number of people who were there. I did not have a very good view as the vehicle just stopped briefly. It was not possible to reach such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put an additional question, Mr. Lukic. Why did the car stop briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, the vehicle stopped because of the commotion on the road and other vehicles that were coming and different persons who were on both sides of the road, including cameramen, journalists, and other vehicles in front, and due to the impossibility to get through without stopping briefly because of the driving in a column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now briefly go back to the 11th of July. We are going to watch the a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of Ms. Stewart, could we please see V000-9265 from 24 minutes, 46 seconds, to 30 minutes. That's a bit more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So please watch this and then I'll ask you something afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we stop for a sec.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The man who is congratulating General Mladic, that is you; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who proffered his hand now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the president of the municipality, Milanco Pajic [phoen], on my left side. I'm the one with the white ribbon tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll take a look at another video-clip as well, the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] V000-9265, from 31 minutes, 24 seconds, to 31 minutes, 54 seconds, that's half a minute. [In English] Can we start now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see in these video-clips that General Mladic persistently insists that they go straight to Bratunac the same moment you are cautioning him. Vinko Pandurevic is cautioning him as well. However, he continues to insist, right? That is what you recall from the field?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is obvious from this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that day, was it possible to get to Bratunac? Is it correct that it was impossible to get through Potocari because of the fighting that was taking place?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assessment of Pandurevic, probably. I was not assessing that area because I did not have a task to go through town that morning. I was supposed to secure, I think, the western hills, the hills on the west side and that was my task, and that's why I said to him that my task was not to go through Potocari to Bratunac. It wasn't that it was -- that I was supposed to go through Potocari as such. I mean, it was just the direction that was specified. Potocari then Bratunac. Obviously Vinko Pandurevic who had already had some insight into what was going on in Potocari, then he cautioned that one should not go to Potocari. That Potocari should be avoided, let me put it that way, because of the people who had assembled there at the base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just for my understanding, the last observations by the witness, did I miss something or is that not specifically found in the video-clip that was played?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last -- what the witness said is -- let me see. It's about Vinko Pandurevic "cautioned that one should not go to Potocari ... Potocari should be avoided ..." Is that audible or have I missed something in the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's not audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's not on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to briefly save some time, perhaps the witness could identify what a Browning is that Mr. Pandurevic refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that assists. I thought a Browning to be a weapon that -- is that -- what is a Browning, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my knowledge, a Browning is an anti-aircraft machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We pronounce it slightly different. In the Serbian we say "Browing."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I would like to have a little question. Your question that triggered the witness's answer at page 9, lines 4 to 14, you said: "On that day, was it possible to get to Bratunac? Is it correct that it was impossible to get through Potocari because of the fighting that was taking place?" Was there fighting taking place?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will verify that. Obviously the witness gave another reason, but I asked him, he would -- he answered the way he answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm asking you: Is it your position that there was fighting taking place at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes -- well not at Potocari, but in between Srebrenica and Potocari it wasn't safe to pass. That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I've to ask you this: Except for the fact that there were people in Potocari, you said that Vinko Pandurevic suggested not to go through Potocari because of them. Could one still hear shooting? Was there still combat under way?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sporadically. You could hear firing and it didn't lead me to a conclusion that there was intensive fighting. I don't know though why there was still some shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at another excerpt, because I wanted to ask you precisely about shootings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to V000-9265, 32 minutes, 37 seconds, to 33 minutes, 12 seconds. [In English] Can we start please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you present when fire was opened on General Mladic in Srebrenica on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not continue moving along with his group. As you could see in one portion of the footage, I was trying to establish contact with my part of the unit and I joined them. In other words, I no longer stayed in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have some indirect knowledge as to who opened fire at General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From some later conversations on the 3rd day, and especially on the 13th when I found myself again in Srebrenica in the morning, and I noted it down in my diary, not my knowledge in terms of opening fire but the fact that I was in town -- sorry, it was the 12th in the morning when I directed my fighters to engage at the last part of the task, and I noted down that there was a lot of plundering. And then the commanding officers who met in town commented yesterday that fire had been opened at General Mladic as he was moving through Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move on to Zepa and ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The simple answer to the question would have been: I don't know. The question was whether you have indirect knowledge as to who opened fire. I mean, that fire was opened was already visible on these -- so the simple answer would have been no. At least in your answer you give no further clue as to who did it. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us move on. In the environs of Zepa you saw General Ratko Mladic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw him for the first time on the 19th of July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you could jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Lukic repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited by the interpreters to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you see General Mladic at Boksanica? Or perhaps correct me if you remember something else.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: I saw General Mladic in one situation. As I was moving to Zepa in a vehicle, I encountered him on a road where he took part providing assistance and advice on how to pullout a UN armoured combat vehicle out of a ditch. That was the first time I saw him I believe. The second time was in the settlement itself in Zepa. When I went down there. He was with another group of officers such as Colonel Andric and others. We met there, exchanged a few words, greeted, and I turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you set out to -- for Zepa, on the 12th or the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My unit and I went to Zepa on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You wanted to ask that your unit be replaced, but you couldn't do that for as long as there was combat; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who at the end did you ask that your unit be rotated or changed? Or let me put it this way: Is it true that you asked General Krstic that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked of General Krstic to approve that my unit be replaced in Zepa; however, he disagreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of intelligence did you have in terms of what ABiH forces were present in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the contents of the brief tasks that were issued as early as Viogor, an assessment was stated to me that there were around 1200 members of the Zepa Brigade present awaiting us in the implementation of our following -- further task. Another assessment was that there were additional 700 soldiers from Srebrenica who managed to break through to the area of Zepa, so up to 2.000 armed men or fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the order to attack the enclave of Zepa of the 13th of July, 1995, was anything changed in terms of treatment of UNPROFOR members and civilians, or were the instructions and orders the same as in the order pertaining to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the treatment of civilians and UNPROFOR, there were no changes. The requests and orders were still in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see in e-court 65 ter number 4103.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted you to get acquainted with the document. Let's look at the heading. It is an order of the Drina Corps command from the forward command post at Krivace dated the 13th of July, 1995; correct? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "Order to attack the Zepa enclave, Operation Number 1."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 3 in the B/C/S and 4 in the English version of this document. Page 3 in the B/C/S, I apologise. Page 3 in the B/C/S, please, because on this page we see 4 at the top. Can we go to the previous page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just below item (c), the second paragraph, it reads: [As read] "The civilian Muslim population and UNPROFOR are not the targets of our operations. Gather them and keep them under guard and crush and destroy armed Muslim groups." Did you abide by this order of the Drina Corps command in the field?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Any changes were not done and were not required.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in the field, this order was not changed in terms of any other oral orders being issued subsequently?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this order did not change.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that fire was opened from an UNPROFOR APC on your forces from the Borak position?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Since I am finished with this document, I seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D290, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In e-court we need 1D978.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will have on the screen an ABiH document. We see that the document is dated the 16th of July, 1995. The tenth line from the top of the page you will find the following sentence: "We are disarming UNPROFOR in accordance with the directive we received earlier." The document is signed by Commander Avdo Palic. Did you have occasion to see that UNPROFOR weaponry exchanged hands in Zepa; that is to say, that it ended up with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, you believed that UNPROFOR opened fire at you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was my belief at the time that it was UNPROFOR engaging us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted too as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D291, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D291 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next can we have 1D794 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1D974.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is a document of the Drina Corps command dated the 24th of July, 1995. It contains intelligence information on the enemy in the Zepa and Gorazde enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to the bottom of the first page in the B/C/S and in the English as well, although we'll have to move to page 2 in the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Counting from the bottom of the page, it is the 16th line in the B/C/S. It reads: "Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You asked for the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First page in the English version. It's sixth line from the bottom of the page. "In any case ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So: "In any case for four days now the Muslims have been making their presence known with heavy 14.5-mm anti-aircraft machine-guns (which were at 00/as printed). Reserve ammunition was at about 25.000 to 30.000 rounds, likewise, coaxial 7.62-mm light machine-guns of the PKT type, with around 40.000 rounds, were probably also dismounted from the OT. The Ukrainian check-points also had 40-mm hand-held rocket-launchers of the RGP type of nine pieces in total. 3 RBR were equipped with nine tactical devices. They had at least 12.040 MM rockets in their reserves. By seizing the personal weapons and equipment of UN personnel, the Muslims probably acquired the following firearms." My question is: In the course of fighting around Zepa, were your units exposed to the action of such weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We could feel their operation for a few days. It was impossible to approach the facility where the APC and the observation post of UNPROFOR forces was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads here that PAMs, P-A-M-s, what are they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we go to the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have to go to the first page in the English version now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Somewhere around the middle you will see is sentence: "The firing system of defence ..." It says here that: "The Muslim forces have also incorporated UNPROFOR combat hardware and weapons which they obtained following the recent blockade and capture of the Ukrainian check-points into their defensive arsenal. We believe that at least nine OT with the accompanying weapons and ammunition are in the hands of the Muslim soldiers." First of all, what is this "OT," do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This abbreviation, "OT," is used for an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that at that time in the area around Zepa the Muslim forces captured the posts of the Ukrainian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was referred to, but my personal estimate is that up until it was all over it was UNPROFOR that was firing and it seemed quite impossible for that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'd like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D974 becomes D292, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the absence of any objections, D292 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need the second page of this document, although we've already admitted it. The third paragraph towards the bottom of the paragraph, and it's paragraph 4 on page 2 of the English version. There is a reference to the civilian population. So in B/C/S the third paragraph towards the bottom. In the English version it's page 2, paragraph 4, towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "The civilian population was mostly evacuated towards the central part of the enclave, Sijamici plateau [phoen], Zepske Kolibe, Debelo Brdo." At the time did you know that the civilian population had been evacuated from the combat zone?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time being we won't be needing this document anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one additional question in this context. You said that you didn't know that the civilian population was mostly evacuated towards the central part of the enclave. Talking about Zepa, was that part of what you were ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received the following order -- I mean, if you mean the document that I saw, the order to attack the enclave and the estimated forces that await us in that area. I did not expect -- or rather, I did not know where the civilian population was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not whether you knew where they were at the time, but my question was what you were ordered to do with the civilian population in Zepa, because you said: "I didn't know that they were mostly evacuated to the central part of the enclave." My question is: What had been your instructions, what had been your orders, in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in accordance with what we had been asked to do; namely, act in a way that would not harm the civilian population or the UN forces, so a correct attitude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to harm them is one, but what were you supposed to do with them, I mean, even if not in a harmful way? Was it leave them at home or leave them -- what was your instruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the area of defence that was organised by the Zepa Brigade, my conclusion, or rather, the conclusion of the person who was issuing the task was that in the deployment of combat forces there is certain, you know, civilian population. Now, where that unit is that -- where that unit that is conducting the defence moved its civilian population so that they would not be in harm's way during combat, I did not think about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, what you thought about -- what was the order you received in relation to the civilian population? What to do with them apart from not harming them, et cetera, but what were you supposed to do with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were supposed to inform the superior command that is in charge of the operation that we came across a group of civilians in the village or in a house and that they should take them over from the area where combat is taking place, and then they should organise their removal from the combat zone, if we do come across such persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if I read in the order that you were ordered to collect them together and to keep them under guard, that is not what you remember to have been your order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Today I did read that but I did not have an opportunity of acting in this way. That's why I don't remember it. I did not come across any civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not what you did. My question was what you were ordered to do, and for one reason or another you now tell me that you remember that you read that in the order a second ago because you said: "Today I did read that ..." So it's totally unclear to me why you apparently avoid answering a direct question in this respect where you reviewed the order a minute ago and apparently had read this. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. At the same time, I see that it's perhaps time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe just to clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This order, did it pertain to the total population of Zepa or only civilians that you come across during combat?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order pertained to the entire population of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The agreement on the population was reached only later, what would happen to the entire population; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're going to deal with that after the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking audible, no gestures, Mr. Mladic. We'll take a break and we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is being brought in, just to bring to the Chamber's attention if it hasn't seen the e-mail that we sent that we will be making an application to add the protective measure of voice distortion. Mr. Lukic informs me that he believes he will be busy this entire session, and then I believe we have some redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it may not arise until next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I would suggest that in case we might decide for that that already, perhaps, preparations are made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not object. Then that's the more reason, then, to already prepare, perhaps not yet but next session but that everybody is ready then to prepare for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll just have to go back to D290 very briefly. Could we please have it in e-court. I don't know whether this is due to language differences, but I'm going to try to get a clarification from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, you see which document this is. We've gone back to the order of the command of the Drina Corps of the 13th of July, 1995, to attack the Zepa enclave in both documents. Since the third page is as the fourth one in e-court. So in both documents we need the fourth page in e-court. We need that part below letter C, the second paragraph of C where it says: "The civilian Muslim population and UNPROFOR are not targets of our operations. Collect them together and keep them under guard ..." Does this order mean that UNPROFOR and civilians should be taken prisoner, or does it mean that they should be given protection? How do you understand this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that this is very clear. Collect them, provide them with protection. But if you're asking about UNPROFOR, it is protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about civilians, protect or take prisoner?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's clear here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not understand Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand you, Mr. Lukic. Could you please repeat what you just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the same go for the population and for UNPROFOR? So does the same go for the population and UNPROFOR, that both should be collected and secured or should they be collected and arrested?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The language here uses the verb "collect" and that has nothing to do with "taken prisoner." "Secure," "obezbedjenje," is "protection," quite simply.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would you like to have the translation reviewed because that's not what the translation is. Then you should ask for it and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we'll see whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think there is some confusion in English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your question is whether "keep them under guard" is the accurate translation of the original. This will be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have a suggestion. My translation, how I understand it, and it can be verified, is "protect by guard."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do understand that that's your translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It can be verified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's probably why there was a confusion before. There is a slight difference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in between English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole thing is I asked what the orders were and the witness did not respond to that. And that they had to be collected, for example, appears not to be in dispute. He didn't say a word about that and that is apparently part of the order as well. But we'll have the translation, and we'll ask specific attention to the fact whether "keep them under guard" should be understood as to "protect them by providing guards to them," or whether it is just plainly as it is translated now into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we'll have to interpret that for ourselves. We have to -- that will be done. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I just for a clarification, not in relation to the guarding of the population, but can you explain how you understood the word "collect them together," how to collect civilian population? What was the idea behind? By which means should that happen, to collect civilian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that they should be kept in a certain area, kept. They should be enabled to stay in a certain area which has a guard service; that is to say, has guards. So it is surrounded by guards so soldiers cannot approach the area; that is to say, soldiers who collected them. That is to say, soldiers who are not guards, and they cannot leave either until a report is sent to superiors and until they are sent to a certain place from that area. So they are provided with protection and they are grouped in a certain area that has around its boundaries some guards. It doesn't have to be a building. It can just be an area, an open area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And how did you carry out this task at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to me personally and to my unit, or generally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not in that situation in the area of Zepa. I did not get into that kind of situation. But in the area of Srebrenica, yesterday when speaking about my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I'm not talking of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- treatment of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, not asking about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am not asking you about Srebrenica. I've got the information I wanted to get. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to move on in relation to the Zepa operation. You marked the direction in which you were moving by burning hay stacks; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the direction and the lines that we reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why was that done?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply that's what was necessary because of the terrain where the combat is taking place. It was necessary to show someone on the other hill where the line was, or rather, where the soldiers were that had reached that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since some houses were set on fire you were asked to identify the perpetrators and punish them; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You ascertained that no member of your unit was engaged in it and you so reported to your superiors; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also reported it to General Krstic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I reported it to the forward command post where he was by communications. I reported it to the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At some point in time an agreement was signed with the Muslim side in Zepa on the cessation of hostilities, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go back to one of your previous questions and the answers to that. You said it was necessary to mark the direction in which you were moving by burning haystacks. That's how I understood your testimony. In order to achieve that, to mark the direction in which you were moving, should it be haystacks or could it be any other small type of fire which would do less damage to the owners of the terrain? I'm wondering what makes it necessary to use haystacks for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to be brief and clear. We were not marking the direction but only the point which we reached. The area was such that there was a lot of hay around in piles in the area where the Zepa cottages were. That was only way, the only means that could be used. Something that could be easily set on fire in order to show where the line was where the unit is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand. I understand the haystack to be the place where the hay is put together in order to be saved for later nourishing the cattle. Is that what we both understand to be a haystack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And some fire with some little pieces of wood, et cetera, would not do? You have to burn a haystack in order to indicate where you are? Is that your testimony, that that is necessary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there were no trees. These were meadows, fields that one could come up to and people simply gathered hay. It was in the area of the Zepa cottages. It is quite a large area of land where grass had been cut and hay was stacked together in piles. There was nothing else one could set on fire. It would have been dangerous to set a tree on fire because it could reach the forest; however, stacks of hay could be controlled in terms of containing the fire. Let me add this: Those haystacks were far from big.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These were not haystacks close to the houses, to the farms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the area of Zepske Kolibe, the Zepa cottages, is specific to the area of Zepa. It is in a valley where the settlements are, and there is 500 metres difference in altitude. Up on top there is a plateau called Zepske Kolibe. There were meadows there where people held livestock and gathered hay in those pastures. In summer-time the livestock was let loose on the pastures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the agreement was signed, the Muslim forces in Zepa continued fighting; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under the agreement, the civilian population was supposed to be transported out of the Zepa enclave according to the agreement signed by the Serbian and Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how we, the subordinate officers, were informed of how it should take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I don't remember any agreement concerning Zepa to be in evidence, so therefore it's difficult for me to follow and evaluate the -- but it may be that I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, I don't think that it's in the evidence, but this witness obviously has no knowledge about the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you ask questions about it, then, of course, we may be interested in [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's part of the 65 ter, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as you're aware, Zepa is very intimately linked to Srebrenica in many ways, and therefore I've not objected thus far. At the same time, the central issues he's bringing up are rather significant and would take many months in a courtroom to sort out. I don't intend to try to do that on redirect, and I won't go into some of them, but I just wanted to alert you to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not insisting on anything, but if any further -- you want the Chamber to pay any further attention to an agreement about which you are asking questions, then, of course, we'd like to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you would like to leave it to this then--

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm leaving exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am just going to show one video that is in the evidence, that's Srebrenica trial video. We need V000-9265. And I would again ask the assistance of Ms. Stewart. We need that video from 32 minutes, 37 seconds, up to 33 minutes, 12 seconds. Can we start. Oh, sorry, wrong numbering. We need V000-9268, 6 minutes, 15 seconds, up to 7 minutes, 48 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning this, let me ask you the following: Did you know that the transport was organised, among others, by UNPROFOR as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were not present when it was taking place; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't present. But I did encounter some of the vehicles transporting the people as I was going to Zepa that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was this organised? Do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think after the signing on the 19th or the 20th, after the subordinates had received information that there was a truce and that evacuation of the population would ensue as well as the disarming of the forces of the Zepa Brigade, and the route was Siversko [phoen] and Rogatica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the civilians left -- after the civilians left, you told us already that the armed forces of the ABiH did not surrender and fighting continued. Your task was to break through via Zepske Kolibe; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received my task to continue in the direction of the Borak and Zepske Kolibe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the course of that operation you were wound?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the last day of fighting, the 29th of July, just below Zlovrh. That is where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the Zepa operation, some documents were issued by your unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at 65 ter 25715.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm informed that there is no translation in e-court available. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are not going through the substance of the documents. I will just check the source and the signature, actually, and the person who allegedly signed the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's final. But nevertheless the Chamber of course would like to know what the content of the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one hard copy with me if it can help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A translation or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in English. Yes, if a translation exists it should be uploaded, but for this moment we could work on the basis of a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the Prosecutor's 65 ter number document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, then, of course, it's for the Prosecution to upload their translation. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's being done, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At this very moment, I take it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see this document in the language we both read and write. Let me ask you the following: Was this document issued by the unit you were in command of?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was issued on the 15th of July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the document, we see your name typed out since this was obviously a telegram. Such documents are not signed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent by telegram, this report, to the Drina Corps command and not the forward command post. It was sent from the command post of my brigade, and the commander's name is typed up as the person responsible for the document. It is not signed. It is a regular report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The command of your unit at the time was in Knezina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were not in Knezina on the 15th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were in the area of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there with a part of the unit which was engaged in implementing the tasks directed at the Zepa enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of Zepa. It was customary, then, to place your name at the bottom of the document as the commander, although you were not included in the drafting of this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The reason for it was that it was a regular combat report which was sent daily concerning events in the area of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document that is on the screen, the regular combat report, let me ask you this: It was not sent to the Main Staff of the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think it was. It is stated here that it went to the Drina Corps command, to our superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was standard procedure?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is important to note that the commander is cited for security reasons due to the possibility of electronic surveillance, thus making it impossible for the enemy to know that the commander is absent from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You, as the brigade commander, were not in direct contact with the Main Staff of the VRS as part of the chain of command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the sense of performing combat operations. However, when it comes to the responsibility for the situation in the area around the Main Staff, given the fact that the area where the Main Staff and the command post and the rear command post was in the area of defence of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, in that regard we did report on certain events in the area of Defence because the brigade, in addition to other units, was responsible for the security and safety of the Main Staff and command post area and possible access to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that regard your brigade was characteristic as compared to the other brigades of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in territorial terms it was almost in the area of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. However, in terms of functionality it was under command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about directives. We'll just be discussing Directive 7 and Directive 7/1, and in relation to that, a document of the Drina Corps that has to do with the beginning of the operation regarding Srebrenica. First of all, as for the character of the directive as a document itself, I would like to ask you whether it is correct that the directive is not a binding document, an executive document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it is very likely that parts of a directive are never actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Directives are documents that pertain to a longer period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether any of this has already been admitted into evidence, but I need Directive 7, 65 ter 4001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. You will recall that the Krivaja 95 attack plan did cite to Directive 7 and 7/1 as the witness testified. I asked him if he received it. He said he did not. And if he is now going to be testifying regarding his opinion regarding directives and those sorts of issues, if it's brief I will not object, but if he's going to be testifying as an expert I would ask the questions not to be leading and that it to be fairly limited in nature because that has not been addressed to us in any form or any report or anything like that. To the degree he actually has knowledge that he received at the time, of course, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any objections against what Mr. McCloskey suggests to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will -- I will not ask for expert opinions. I will just compare what the various documents encompass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness has any knowledge about it because comparing documents, the Chamber is perfectly able to do that. Unless you have any specific factual questions of which the witness, who apparently has not seen this document before, whether he has any specific knowledge about matters in the document. Then perhaps you first start with asking about his knowledge, and only then proceed if there is any need to do so with the documents and the possible --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are some factual actual questions I just checked, but before we have to introduce them. Just small parts of

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey -- keep it short so as for Mr. McCloskey not to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Able to bear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- start objecting. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have Directive 7 before us. We accept that you haven't seen it, but I would just briefly like to take you to -- well, actually, I don't know what it's like in e-court but the document I have has an empty page after each printed page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'd like to take a look at page 15 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In e-court there are no empty pages. In e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe there are, maybe there are not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 8 in e-court. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise. I think it's clear from the record that he said he did not receive this document, that at this date in time it's hard to imagine that he has not seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's wait and see what questions Mr. Lukic will put to the witness, but perhaps we clarify. Have you seen the document before, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in English version we need page 10. The part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the -- oh, it's back now. The B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are just going to discuss this part that has to do with the Drina Corps. This part of Directive 7 that was issued by the Supreme Command of the armed forces of Republika Srpska says that the operation regarding Srebrenica and Zepa should be carried out in co-ordination with the SRK, that's the Sarajevo Romanija Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the ground, while operations were carried out, was there co-operation with the Sarajevo Romanija Corps or was it only the Drina Corps that carried out this operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this operation of Srebrenica and Zepa, it was only the Drina Corps that independently carried this out with its own forces, these activities that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct that the Drina Corps could choose what the most favourable way of carrying out this operation would be because they did it on their own?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conclusion is based on this: Through their active defence, so it's not that attacks were planned here, active defence of the Drina Corps and thus improve positions, and so on, not to read this further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the Drina Corps did not wait for the Main Staff to bring together the activities of the SRK and the Drina Corps. Is that what you saw in the field?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, as for e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- you move to another page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you testified that what we read here, that it was for the Drina Corps itself to decide in which way to achieve what was apparently intended. Could you tell me what the various choices are, what the various ways are to achieve what is written in the last three lines; that is: "By planned and well-thought-out combat operations, create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." Could you tell us what your options were to the various choices you had to achieve this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to respond from the level of a brigade commander. I said that I saw the document but I did not receive it then when it was written in 1995 and after it was made public, so I was not thinking about this. It was the corps command that assessed how this should be done, and obviously their assessment was that by separating and narrowing the area of the enclaves would influence the population. And then they would demand from their civilian and military leadership to have contact with the other side and that they would save themselves in this way but by not being prisoners of their own leaders. That would be the basis of my thinking on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's rather unclear to me. How would they save themselves? By leaving, is that what you mean to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they don't have to leave but their status could be changed in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would that create a situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life? You are giving a picture where life would still be bearable for them in the area and that seems not to be what is intended here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed? Have you finished your question? Can I just add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This sentence, Mr. President, this sentence was uttered in a somewhat different way as compared to the terminology that is used by forces that are preparing to topple regimes in different parts of the world. These are sanctions, just phrased differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is that your interpretation of the document? Where does it come from that you say this is what was meant despite the clear language of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I haven't received this document, but I believe - it is my understanding of this - that these different activities through combat activities and through narrowing the area of the enclaves and interrupting communication between the two enclaves, the population should have a growing awareness of them being, in a way, prisoners of their own leaders and that, therefore, these leaders should be changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be the meaning of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You give the document a meaning which I have difficulties in reconciling with the text of the document. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the first page of this document again in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you can see, it's clear to you, too -- but let us explain this for us lay people that do not find all of this clear. This document was compiled by the Supreme Command of the armed forces of Republika Srpska. This is a body that is different from the Main Staff of Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's leading and it's absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you refrain from leading, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm doing cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He knows very well that this document was compiled by the Main Staff, drafted by General Miletic, the chief of operations of General Mladic, and went through each of his assistant commanders, and to say otherwise is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are at this moment in cross-examination but you are eliciting evidence in support of your own case rather than in -- rather than that you're challenging and testing the evidence which was produced by the Prosecution. Under those circumstances, it's appropriate to refrain from leading. And before we -- you ask any further questions about how this document came about, you should first establish whether the witness has any knowledge of it going beyond what the document itself says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is written in this document? What or who is the source of this document, could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what the source of the document is according to the text, the Chamber can read. So therefore, there is no reason to ask the witness about that. The document reads at the top that it comes from the Supreme Command of the armed forces of Republika Srpska and I take it that the witness is not -- has not a better ability of reading that the Chamber has.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for having that on the record. Can we see the last page of the document, please. There are empty pages here. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's not the last page of the document. We have to go two pages ahead and this is only the letter that was sent with the main document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This last page just cannot -- [Microphone not activated], sorry, this last page does tell us drafted by Colonel Radivoje Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no. We'll get to that as well. This is the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last page in e-court is -- apparently we are not talking about -- are we talking about one document or more documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously there are two documents in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where does the second document start in e-court, Mr. Lukic, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you want to look at the first page and then at the last page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then of course that--

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- the last page of this document, not of the e-court document. I'm not interested about the e-court now. I want to see the last page of the documents on our screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's what page in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are empty pages. I thought that there were. And we can see, and it's very hard to follow, and I can count them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I have e-court in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the first page of this document. I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar can help us, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's page 21 in B/C/S and page 15 in English version in the e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And these are on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are on the screen, yes. Thank you. Since there are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I nevertheless would very much like to identify exactly what we have. I have on page 1 in e-court, I have a document which apparently originates from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska, very urgent, directive for upcoming operations --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Directive for upcoming operations sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Lukic. I am not finished yet. Directive for upcoming operations. Enclosed with this document we are sending you the directive for further operations number 7. Okay. That is signed by the Chief of Staff Manojlo Milovanovic. That's the first page. Then on the second page I look at what is a document which apparently originates from the Supreme Command of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, special defence, state secret. That is the document you showed us a minute ago and of which I said the Chamber is able to read what its origin is. Then the following pages seem all to be still part of that document which starts at page 2 in e-court, and that document ends on page 15 - so it's not a letter but it is the document apparently sent through that letter by -- signed and stamped Supreme Commander, Dr. Radovan Karadzic. And just above that it says: "Drafted by Colonel Radivoje Miletic, typed by staff sergeant Spasoje Zeljkovic." That is what we have in e-court. One-page letter, one in English, 14-page document, apparently coming from that Supreme Command, signed by Mr. Karadzic, drafted, as the document says, by Colonel Radivoje Miletic and typed by Zeljkovic. That's what we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English version. In B/C/S version first comes document and then cover letter. So that's the confusion. There are empty pages as well. So it's very hard to follow this document, the Prosecutor's document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently - and that seems to be the dispute - who drafted the document which was issued by the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will cover that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But that apparently was the issue and we could ask the witness whether he has any knowledge about it. And if the order of the documents in B/C/S is different from English in e-court, then that should be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We cannot change it. It's a Prosecutor's document -- Prosecution document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And to clarify the point, Mr. Lukic is correct. This is, as you know, the ERN process and so it got ERN'd in the -- in this different order than it is from the B/C/S and the English. So that's created the sort of glitch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has no empty pages. It has the back of the pages, I take it, with ERN stamps on it. But that is to be clarified. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed. Apparently Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking, microphone off, whispering.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, let me ask you this: There is a reference to someone drafting the directive and the person in question is Radivoje Miletic. Was Radivoje Miletic Ratko Mladic's assistant or was he an operative in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is leading, so what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said before that if you want to elicit evidence in support of your own case, not testing the evidence presented by the Prosecution, that it would be appropriate from refraining from leading; that is, the two different subject matters which can be touched upon in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the position of Radivoje Miletic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Colonel Miletic was the chief of the operations organ in the Main Staff. In other words, he was subordinated to the Chief of Staff, General Milovanovic. He was not an assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to find Directive 7/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter number 5821 received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if we move to Directive 7/1, perhaps it would be better to take a break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, may I inquire as far as time is concerned where you are?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am informed that I have 50 minutes left but I'll probably finish in less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether you had all that time left is still to be seen, but if you finish in half an hour the Chamber accepts that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said 15 or 50?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. My comment was on what I heard, that is about 50. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We saw that Colonel Miletic drafted Resolution 7. As regards documents of that kind, is it the person drafting it that is responsible for it or is it the person who signs it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I need to remind you of the duty held by Colonel Miletic. He was the chief of the operations organ. This document in terms of its content was not the result of Colonel Miletic's thought process --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decisions and positions presented therein --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the question simply was about, as Mr. Lukic said, kind of documents, I take it that he refers to directives or similar, whether it is the person drafting who bears final responsibility or whether it's the person signing. That's the question. Which of the two -- or, if there is any third option, tell us, but do not start testifying about the content of the document. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. You said "final responsibility" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I am not sure Mr. Lukic did, but responsibility is an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to -- I should phrase the question exactly as Mr. Lukic did it in this respect, and I'll re-read what it was. Let me see. The question is: "These kind of documents, is it the person drafting it that is responsible for it or is it the person who signs it?" Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wanted to say that Colonel Miletic did not draft this document. It did not put it together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He is responsible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can answer the question now whether he drafted it or not. Do you have any personal knowledge about who drafted it? Were you there when it was drafted? Then please tell us. Simple question: Were you there when it was drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terms of the content of the document, it is the person signing it who is responsible; that is to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my question. Mr. Lukic, that's the question you -- I think you put to the witness. If there are any follow-up questions, of course you are free to put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the ideas and thoughts and concepts of the person belonged to the person signing the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is classic expert testimony which I don't mind, but I would like it, in this case, to be leading -- not -- not because he's necessarily bringing out his case, which I think is find, but because this is well beyond his case.
